input.quote: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.
input.rationale: Section 7 is captioned "Indemnification of Contractor," but the section body (p0035-p0037) contains only liability caps, a consequential-damages waiver and a mutual attorneys' fees waiver - there is no operative indemnity language. Document-wide searches for "indemnif" return only the Section 7 heading itself, and "hold harmless" returns nothing; Sections 4 and 5 contain no defence obligation either. The closest protection is the Section 5(c) non-infringement warranty (p0026), which is a bare representation: it gives us a damages claim for breach but no right to have RadialSpark defend or fund a third-party infringement suit against us, and any such warranty claim is capped at fees paid under Section 7(a). That fails even the fallback (Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions and remedies) and sits in walk-away territory of "no Vendor IP indemnity at all." Notably, Section 7(a) carves "Paragraph 9" out of Contractor's cap, but Paragraph 9 is Independent Contractor status - a dangling cross-reference suggesting an indemnity clause was intended and dropped in drafting. We inserted the preferred vendor indemnity as a new Section 7(d) covering IP infringement, breach of law, Contractor-caused data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation and a carve-out from the Section 7(a) cap and Section 7(c) fees waiver so the defence obligation is not read as capped at fees paid. No Customer indemnity exists, so there is nothing to narrow on our side. The fallback (IP-only indemnity with modification/combination exclusions and a 3x annual fees super-cap) is offered in the comment as a landing zone.

proposal.summary: Insert a Contractor (Vendor) indemnity covering third-party IP infringement, breach of law, Contractor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard claim procedure and carve-out from the § 7(a) cap.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 7 is titled "Indemnification of Contractor" but the Agreement contains no indemnity at all, and the Section 5(c) non-infringement warranty gives us no right to a defence if a third party sues us over the Works. We have added a Contractor indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, Contractor-caused data incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with a standard notice-and-control procedure; if you prefer, we can narrow this to the IP indemnity with the usual modification/combination exclusions and a 3x annual fees super-cap.

ops.text: (d) Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Services or the Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (ii) Contractor's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company data or Confidential Information caused by Contractor; or (iv) Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Company shall provide Contractor with prompt written notice of the claim, sole control of the defense and settlement thereof (provided that Contractor shall not settle any claim in a manner that imposes any obligation or admission on Company without Company's prior written consent), and reasonable cooperation at Contractor's expense. Contractor's obligations under this Section 7(d) shall not be subject to the limitation of liability set forth in Section 7(a), and the waiver of attorneys' fees in Section 7(c) shall not apply to this Section 7(d).
